column3: Use when consolidating a product or dividing an authorized change into reviewable deliveries.
Use when changes cross many modules, rules repeat, dependencies cycle or domain ownership is unclear.
Use when functions mix business decisions, low-level details and effects at incompatible levels.
Use when module names, locations or public APIs obscure responsibilities that are already understood.
Use when unfinished features, abandoned paths or competing implementations make a codebase ambiguous.
Use when revisions, previews, selections or generated artifacts are associated with the wrong version.
Use when layers disagree about data, rules are duplicated or a write leaves records inconsistent.
Use when a working interface lacks product-specific hierarchy, identity or visual coherence.
Use when spacing, alignment or information density makes a screen hard to scan or use.
Use when users lose context or need unnecessary steps to complete a multi-screen task.
Use when mobile navigation, browser history or layouts fail across phone and wide-screen sizes.
Use when a simple selection or adjustment requires excessive forms and disconnected controls.
Use when controls, forms, dialogs or asynchronous changes may exclude keyboard or assistive-technology users.
Use when teams repeat interface mistakes or create incompatible component and token variations.
Use when measured latency, freezes, excessive work or rendering cost affects a real workflow.
Use when progress stalls, success appears too early or stale asynchronous results overwrite current state.
Use when agent jobs, queues, workers and model capacity are conflated or incorrectly accounted for.
Use when bots or notifications fail, repeat or produce unexplained message volume.
Use when an integration looks configured but required steps or operational readiness remain unclear.
Use when an offering is presented without evidence that its exact variant and destination are supported.
Use when previews or generated assets lack clear source, version, orientation or ownership.
Use when totals, model costs or operational metrics have unclear scope, origin or meaning.
Use when alerts repeat, historical incidents look current or acknowledging an alert appears to resolve it.
Use when simulation, training or demo flows share code and data paths with real operations.
Use when duplicated tests slow maintenance without protecting distinct failure modes.
Use when a passing suite misses important bugs or the required regression coverage is unclear.
Use when reviewing a bounded diff or pull request for actionable defects and regressions.
Use when a wrong result, exception or intermittent failure has no demonstrated root cause.
Use when untrusted input, credentials, permissions or tenant boundaries may permit unintended access.
Use when stored schemas, identifiers, jobs or public payloads must survive a version change.
Use when validation pipelines lack clear ownership, local/CI parity or predictable command effects.
Use when dependencies, builds or CI fail or behave differently across environments.
Use when checking whether an integrated change actually satisfies its acceptance criteria.
